jobs.title: Forward Deployment AI Engineer
jobs.description:
Lyra Technology Group is a private equity-backed holding company that invests in and operates industry leading technology service businesses. Our companies are operated independently by exceptional management teams. Companies that join our group retain the employees, name, and culture that have made them successful. As a platform of Evergreen Services Group, we never divest from businesses we partner with and approach every decision with the goal of driving sustainable and healthy growth over the long term.  

Forward Deployment AI Engineer

Lyra Technology Group is a group of over 130 managed IT service providers (MSPs) serving over 10,000 clients and managing over 300,000 end user devices across the US, Canada, the UK, Europe, Australia and New Zealand. We're hiring several Forward Deployment AI Engineers (FDEs) to develop and deploy Vega, our proprietary AI Operating System, across our MSP operating companies.

We’re building a team of enterprising, ambitious engineers who are as fulfilled tracking down a tricky bug as they are watching their work transform a business. You’ll drive new feature development and deployment into our operating companies. You’ll be on-site, learning how their teams work, connecting the platform to their systems, changing day-to-day workflows, and proving the impact in dollars.

What You'll Own

Innovation and product: build features across the stack, close integration gaps, and fix what breaks, including a turn on call for production. We’re building from zero to one, and innovation across the stack is a mandate.
Discovery: map how each business works, find the opportunities with the highest return, and flag local solutions worth turning into shared capabilities.
Deployments, end to end: onboard new operating companies, integrate with their tools, and get front-line teams using the platform every day.
Integrations: build connectors to the ticketing systems and other tools our businesses run on, behind one shared layer, so the agents work the same way at each business.
Agentic workflows: design agents with tool use, memory and multi-agent orchestration for triage, enrichment, root-cause analysis and proactive support.
Earning trust: be the technical advisor each customer's leaders and front-line staff rely on, translate AI into business value, and earn the operational changes the platform depends on.
Enablement: train the AI engineers placed at our operating companies, their local AI leads and front-line teams to run the platform day to day and adapt it to their workflows, while you keep owning the product underneath.
Reporting results: set baselines, measure impact and cost, and report to leadership on what's working and what isn't.

Requirements

Adaptability: no business process or requirement is too messy. You have no ego and would be happy shadowing IT techs working in disparate systems for hours on end and leveraging that experience to build organized agent systems.
Communication that fits the audience: you can walk a CFO through benefits and use cases and go deep on implementation with fellow engineers.
A strong track record of shipping software that real users depend on, and owning it after launch.
Hands-on experience working on AWS-hosted systems.
Full-stack fluency in TypeScript/Node and React, or a strong background in another language (Python, Java, C#, Go) and the appetite to switch.
Integration experience with third-party APIs: auth flows, rate limits, webhooks and messy data.
You’ve shipped AI-driven products and have production experience with LLMs, agentic products/features, building evals, and proper governance.
Agentic development tools (Claude Code, Cursor or similar), and the judgment to know when AI-written code is safe to merge.
You don't need to have worked in IT services. You do need to learn an unfamiliar business quickly.

Preferred

Experience in IT services or managed service operations, or with ticketing systems such as ConnectWise, HaloPSA or Autotask.
Relational database depth, and experience keeping each customer's data separate with access control and audit trails.
MCP servers, modern agent frameworks, and security and privacy work such as data residency and PII handling.

Who Thrives Here

You own a number, not just a feature. You set a baseline, measure the impact, and kill what doesn't pay.
You treat cost as a product input. Model spend, compute and per-customer margin are part of your design decisions.
You'd rather build once for many businesses than build bespoke for one.
You find messy problems energizing. Integrations break, data is messy, and the customer's real process rarely matches the documentation.
You're comfortable with ambiguity and a small team, and you'd rather spend a day being scrappy than writing a spec.
You work independently in the field but build as a team. You review each other's code, share what each deployment taught you, and ask for help before a local fix becomes a fork.

Compensation and location

$160,000 - $200,000 base salary (DOE), plus discretionary annual bonus potential. Hybrid, based in our NYC office, with up to 25% travel to operating companies.

If you want to build AI that service-desk teams at over 130 businesses use every day, and be in the room when it lands, we'd like to hear from you!

Lyra Technology Group is an equal opportunity employer. We value diverse perspectives and are committed to building an inclusive team.

You turn design decisions into working solutions: AI-enabled workflows configured on the platform, prototypes users can click through, and integration requirements our integration partners build against. You bring enough business-architecture discipline to understand why a workflow works the way it does before you automate it, and enough technical depth to make the automation real. You work day to day with the Business Analyst and our integration partners, and you’re the person who decides whether a design can actually be built.

Key Responsibilities
· Embed with the agency’s clinical, operational, and IT teams: sit in design sessions, learn the workflow and its constraints, and propose a technical approach on the spot.

· Map the current-state system landscape well enough to design against it: interfaces, data flows, where the data really lives, and which constraints are technical versus policy.

jobs.title: Lead Software Engineer- Agentic Cyber Operations & Platforms
jobs.description:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Lead Software Engineer -Agentic Cyber Operations & Platforms

Help us build the next generation of AI-powered cybersecurity.

What if you could use your software engineering skills to help transform how one of the world's leading insurance companies detects, investigates, and responds to cyber threats?

At Allstate, we're building something new, and we're looking for engineers who want to be part of it.

Our newly established Agentic Cyber Operations & Platforms (ACO&P) organization
is bringing together software engineering, cloud technologies, security data, AI, and automation to create smarter, faster, and more connected cyber defense capabilities.

We're looking for hands-on software engineers who enjoy building solutions, solving complex problems, and working with emerging technologies.

What You'll Be Working On:
We're growing two closely connected engineering teams
. While both share a strong software development foundation, each focuses on a different part of our cybersecurity transformation.

Cyber Data & Intelligence: Build the Foundation

Help us connect the dots across our cybersecurity ecosystem. This team is building the data intelligence and integration capabilities
that bring together security information from different applications, cloud environments, and enterprise platforms.

The team is also building scalable observability and telemetry capabilities that collect, process, enrich, and deliver data across applications, infrastructure, cloud environments, and security platforms.

You'll have opportunities to:

Design and develop software integrations, APIs, and data pipelines that connect multiple security and technology platforms.
Design and evolve observability and telemetry pipelines that ingest data from multiple enterprise sources and enable monitoring, analytics, security intelligence, and automation use cases.
Build solutions to collect, process, and deliver security telemetry and operational data.
Develop automation that makes security information more accessible, reliable, and actionable.
Apply software engineering and DevOps practices to build scalable, secure, and maintainable solutions.
Help establish the foundation for future AI-powered security analytics and intelligent automation.
Help build a unified data intelligence layer that makes security and operational telemetry accessible for advanced analytics, automation, and AI-enabled workflows.

You might be a great fit if: You're a software engineer who enjoys backend development, APIs, systems integration, and working with data, with an interest in observability and modern cloud and platform engineering. Experience with cybersecurity, DevOps, or observability platforms is a plus.

Mission Control: Build the Experience

Help us reimagine how cybersecurity teams manage and respond to incidents. This team is focused on bringing together incident management tools and capabilities into a more connected, streamlined experience for cyber defenders.

You'll have opportunities to:

Engineer and enhance applications that support cybersecurity incident management and response.
Build integrations between enterprise applications and security platforms.
Support and improve existing cloud-based applications while helping develop new in-house solutions.
Take software solutions through the complete development lifecycle, from concept and proof of concept to production.
Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines, automation, and cloud-based application infrastructure.
Help create a unified platform that makes it easier for security teams to investigate, collaborate, and respond to threats.

You might be a great fit if: You're a hands-on backend or full-stack software engineer with experience building applications, working with cloud technologies, and delivering production-ready solutions. Cybersecurity experience is a welcome bonus, not a prerequisite.

Both teams offer opportunities to contribute to a growing engineering organization and help shape how we build and deliver modern cyber operations capabilities.

What We're Looking For

At the heart of this role is strong software engineering capability. We're interested in engineers who can build, integrate, automate, and deliver reliable technology solutions.

The Essentials

Software Engineering: Hands-on experience developing applications, backend services, integrations, or automation solutions using languages such as Python, Java, C#/.NET, JavaScript/TypeScript, or similar.
Application Development & Integration: Experience building or supporting APIs, software integrations, data pipelines, or production applications.
Cloud Technologies: Working knowledge of Azure, AWS, or GCP, along with an understanding of modern infrastructure and application environments.
DevOps & CI/CD: Familiarity with source control, automated testing, deployment pipelines, and software delivery practices using tools such as Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions.
AI-Assisted Development: Experience using AI coding assistants, such as GitHub Copilot, to support software development, with an understanding of code review, testing, and validation.
Security Awareness: An understanding of secure software development principles, including application security, access controls, and protecting sensitive information.
Collaboration: Experience working with cross-functional teams to translate technical requirements into practical engineering solutions.

Experience That Would Be a Plus

Depending on your background and interests, experience in any of the following areas could be valuable:

Cybersecurity & Observability: Experience with observability, telemetry, log processing, security monitoring, or SIEM technologies such as Datadog, Cribl, OpenTelemetry, Azure Monitor, Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, or similar platforms.
Data Engineering & Integration: Working with telemetry and data pipelines, streaming technologies, Azure Data Explorer (ADX), Kusto Query Language (KQL), SQL/NoSQL databases, data lakes, Kafka, Databricks or similar technologies.
Cloud & Platform Engineering: Infrastructure as Code, Terraform, Docker, Kubernetes, and cloud-native application development.
Infrastructure & Observability: Familiarity with cloud infrastructure, networking, distributed systems, observability, telemetry, and modern application architectures.
Full-Stack Development: Building REST APIs, microservices, or web applications using frameworks such as React or Angular.
AI & Intelligent Automation: Exposure to AI/ML technologies, AI agents, agentic workflows, or automation solutions.
Cybersecurity Concepts: Familiarity with vulnerability management, incident response, OWASP, MITRE ATT&CK, or zero-trust principles.

These are preferred skills, not a checklist. We recognize that great engineers bring different technical strengths and experiences. You don't need to have worked with every technology listed to be considered.

Why Join Us?

Build something new: Join a growing organization where you'll help develop foundational platforms and capabilities rather than simply maintain existing systems.
Engineering with real-world impact: Your work will help cybersecurity professionals access better information, make faster decisions, and respond more effectively to emerging threats.
Explore AI and automation : Work in an environment where AI-assisted development and intelligent automation are part of our technology direction, with opportunities to expand your skills as these capabilities evolve.
Bring your strengths and keep growing : Whether your background is in backend development, full-stack engineering, cloud platforms, or data integration, you'll have opportunities to apply your expertise while developing new capabilities.
Collaborate across disciplines: Work alongside software engineers, cloud specialists, data professionals, and cybersecurity teams to solve meaningful technology challenges.

Ready to Build What's Next?

If you're a software engineer who loves solving problems, enjoys building technology from the ground up, and is curious about the intersection of software engineering, cybersecurity, and AI, this could be an exciting next step.

You don't have to come from a traditional cybersecurity background. What matters most is your ability to engineer solutions, learn new technologies, and contribute to building something meaningful.

Bring your engineering expertise. We'll bring the challenges, opportunities, and room to grow.

Skills

Application Development, CI/CD, DevOps, Full Stack Development, Identity Access Management (IAM)

Compensation offered for this role is 100,000.00 - 170,500.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

jobs.title: Principal Machine Learning Architect (E6213)
jobs.description:
Job Summary

The ML Architect is the technical owner of IEEE's enterprise AI/ML Platform on Databricks on AWS, responsible for its architecture and for leading its implementation. This role defines how machine learning models, generative AI solutions, and AI agents move from experimentation into secure, scalable, and well-governed production services, and how applications and systems across the organization consume them. The ML Architect is accountable for the platform's foundations, including account and workspace configuration, Unity Catalog governance, compute and network architecture, infrastructure-as-code, and CI/CD, as well as the services built on those foundations: model deployment and serving, agent orchestration, retrieval and vector search, evaluation, and monitoring. A primary measure of success for this role is productivity of IEEE's data science teams and AI products. The platform is run as a product whose core customers are data scientists, application architecture and developers, cloud and infrastructure engineers. The ML Architect works alongside those teams to shorten the distance between a working prototype and a dependable production capability. The ideal candidate pairs deep, hands-on Databricks and AWS expertise with the judgment to balance cost, performance, security, and speed of delivery, and with the leadership ability to build and direct a blended team of staff and consulting engineers and architects.

The ML Architect will report to the Director of Enterprise Data Science & Data Solutions and will work in close partnership with the data science teams, the enterprise data architecture team, and the networking, security, and cloud infrastructure teams, as well as with the product, application, and business stakeholders who consume AI capabilities. The ML Architect will have latitude to shape the structure of the platform team and to determine the right mix of staff and consultant resources needed to deliver the roadmap.

Key Responsibilities

Serves as the accountable architect for the enterprise AI/ML Platform on Databricks on AWS, setting its technical direction, reference architecture, and multi-year roadmap, and leading its implementation.
Configures and administers the Databricks account and workspaces, including Unity Catalog, identity federation and service principals, compute and cluster policies, serverless options, and separation of development, test, and production environments with the Enterprise Data Architecture team.
Partners with the networking, security, and cloud infrastructure teams to define secure deployment patterns, including customer-managed VPCs, AWS PrivateLink, IAM roles, encryption with customer-managed keys, and secrets management.
Establishes infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD practices, using tools such as Terraform and Databricks Asset Bundles, so that platform components and ML workloads are versioned, repeatable, and auditable.
Designs and implements the MLOps lifecycle, including experiment tracking, model versioning and registration in MLflow and Unity Catalog, automated testing, approval gates, promotion across environments, and rollback.
Takes models and generative AI solutions built by data science teams from prototype to production, delivering services that are reliable, monitored, and supportable.
Architects how models and AI services are consumed at scale, including real-time inference through secured REST endpoints, event-driven integrations that push results to downstream systems, and batch and streaming scoring.
Sets service standards for those interfaces, covering authentication and authorization, versioning, rate limiting, latency and throughput targets, autoscaling, and cost controls.
Designs and builds agent orchestration capabilities, including multi-step and multi-agent workflows, tool and function calling against governed data and services, retrieval-augmented generation with vector search, and state management.
Establishes evaluation, observability, and guardrail practices for AI agents and LLM-based applications, including tracing, offline and online evaluation, human feedback, content safety controls, and usage tracking.
Implements monitoring for production models and AI services covering data and prediction drift, model quality, latency, availability, and spend, with alerting and defined retraining or remediation paths.
Accelerates data science delivery through self-service templates, reference implementations, reusable components, and documentation that shorten the path from experimentation to production.
Works directly with data scientists to understand their workflows and requirements, and prioritizes platform capabilities based on their feedback and on business demand.
Collaborates with the enterprise data architecture team to align the platform with enterprise data models, lakehouse design standards, data governance, lineage, and access policies.
Builds, leads, and develops a platform team of ML engineers, platform engineers, and architects made up of IEEE staff and consultants, and determines the team structure, roles, and staffing mix required to deliver the roadmap.
Directs the work of consulting partners, including defining scope and deliverables, reviewing technical output, and ensuring knowledge transfer so that critical platform IP and know-how remain within IEEE.
Mentors engineers and data scientists on ML engineering and production-readiness practices, and leads architecture and code reviews.
Embeds responsible AI and governance controls into the platform in partnership with security, privacy, and legal stakeholders, including model documentation, access auditing, and alignment with IEEE's AI and data policies.
Manages platform cost and capacity using FinOps practices such as resource tagging, budgets, compute policies, and right-sizing.
Evaluates new Databricks, AWS, and third-party capabilities, runs proofs of concept, and recommends additions to the technology stack.
Communicates platform vision, architecture decisions, and progress to technical and executive audiences, and maintains architecture decision records and reference documentation.

Additional Responsibilities

10% Domestic

Education

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field, or equivalent professional experience Req
Master's or other advanced degree Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Statistics, or another quantitative field Pref

Work Experience

7-10 years Designing, building, and operating machine learning or data platforms in production, including ownership of platform architecture Req
4-7 years Architecting and administering Databricks on AWS, including workspace configuration, Unity Catalog, compute policies, and private networking Req
7-10 years Deploying, serving, monitoring, and maintaining machine learning models in production using MLOps and CI/CD practices Req
Less than 2 years Building and deploying generative AI applications and agentic workflows in production, including evaluation and guardrails Req
4-7 years Designing APIs and event-driven integrations for high-volume services consumed by other applications Req
2-4 years Leading technical teams that include both employees and consultants, including scoping and overseeing vendor deliverables Req
4-7 years Hands-on experience with AWS AI/ML services such as Amazon Bedrock or Amazon SageMaker Pref
4-7 years Hands-on experience with Databricks services Pref

Licenses and Certifications

Databricks certifications (such as Machine Learning Professional) 3 Years Pref
AWS certifications (such as Solutions Architect – Professional) 5 Years Pref

Skills and Requirements

Expert-level knowledge of Databricks on AWS, including Unity Catalog, MLflow, Model Serving, Vector Search, Delta Lake, Jobs/Workflows, and serverless compute.
Strong working knowledge of AWS architecture for ML platforms, including IAM, VPC design, PrivateLink, S3, KMS, Secrets Manager, API Gateway, Lambda, EventBridge, and CloudWatch.
Hands-on experience with agent orchestration frameworks and patterns, such as LangGraph or Databricks agent tooling, including tool calling, retrieval-augmented generation, and multi-agent coordination; familiarity with the Model Context Protocol is a plus.
Proficiency in Python and SQL, and working knowledge of Spark/PySpark; experience with Scala or Java is a plus.
Infrastructure-as-code and DevOps expertise, including Terraform, Databricks Asset Bundles, Git-based development workflows, and CI/CD tooling.
Solid grounding in ML engineering concepts, including feature engineering and feature stores, reproducibility, model versioning, drift detection, and retraining strategies.
Experience designing secure, scalable service interfaces, including REST API design, OAuth 2.0 and token-based authentication, asynchronous and event-driven integration, and load testing.
Understanding of LLM evaluation, observability, and safety techniques, including tracing, automated and human evaluation, prompt and model versioning, and guardrails.
Familiarity with containerization and orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.
Knowledge of data governance, security, and privacy practices for AI systems, including access control, lineage, audit logging, and the handling of sensitive data.
Working knowledge of cost management and FinOps practices for cloud and Databricks consumption.
Proven ability to build, lead, and develop high-performing technical teams, and to manage consultants and vendors against clear deliverables.
Collaborative, service-oriented approach, with the ability to earn the trust of data scientists and partner teams and to run the platform as a product with internal customers.
Ability to explain architectural choices and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, verbally and in writing.

Other Requirements:

As defined in IEEE Policies, individuals currently serving on an IEEE board or committee are not eligible to apply.

PLEASE NOTE: This position is not budgeted for employer-sponsored immigration support, this includes all persons in F (both CPT and OPT), J, H, L, or O status.

This position is dedicated to Enrollment Management, with priorities set jointly between the VPEM, AVP Enrollment Systems & Analytics, and Institutional Research.

Serves as a primary developer of data sources, analytic datasets, and Business Intelligence (BI) solutions that support enrollment management leaders and partners in recruitment, admissions, financial aid, enrollment planning, student success, and related areas.
Partners with Enrollment Systems to acquire, integrate, clean, and validate data from Slate (CRM), PeopleSoft/Campus Solutions (SIS), financial aid, marketing, survey, and external market sources using approved access methods and integrations; documents data lineage and follows institutional data governance standards.
Analyzes and interprets enrollment data using statistical and data science techniques, including regression, classification, clustering, forecasting, machine learning, and other appropriate methods, to identify trends, drivers, risks, and opportunities across the enrollment funnel and among student populations, academic programs, and geographic markets.
Develops, validates, deploys, and monitors predictive models to support enrollment management priorities such as inquiry and application conversion, admission and yield, melt, enrollment forecasting, financial aid strategy, retention, and student persistence.
Builds enrollment forecasts, scenario analyses, and simulations to support goal setting, class shaping, capacity planning, resource allocation, and strategic enrollment planning.
Supports financial aid strategy through net tuition revenue, discount rate, aid leveraging, and price-sensitivity modeling in partnership with Financial Aid and enrollment leadership.
Collaborates with enrollment management leadership to create dashboards, visualizations, and recurring analytic products that communicate key performance indicators, funnel performance, cohort trends, model results, and progress toward enrollment goals.
Works closely with campus partners to understand enrollment-related business questions, translate them into analytic requirements, and develop solutions that are accurate, timely, actionable, and aligned with institutional priorities.
Collaborates with Dean of Admission and Director of Admission to build annual predictive admission model; ensures models undergo fairness review and comply with legal requirements governing the use of student characteristics in admission decisions.
Validates and benchmarks consultant models and builds internal modeling capacity to reduce dependency on external vendors over time.
Evaluates the effectiveness of enrollment strategies, outreach, communications, events, financial aid initiatives, and other interventions using appropriate measurement approaches, and provides findings that can inform future strategy and resource allocation.
Provides technical guidance, mentorship, and code and model review for enrollment management analysts; establishes shared analytic standards, documentation practices, and reusable methods across enrollment analytics.
Communicates analytic methods, assumptions, limitations, and findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences and promotes responsible, transparent, and appropriate use of predictive analytics in enrollment decision-making.
Maintains professional and technical knowledge of data science, enrollment analytics, higher education trends, and relevant technologies by attending educational workshops, reviewing professional publications, and establishing professional networks.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Required Education & Experience

Master’s degree in data science, statistics, or related field
4 years’ experience in data analytics, including data and statistical modeling
Experience working with higher education data

OR

6 years’ experience in data analytics, including data and statistical modeling
Experience working with higher education data

Preferred Education & Experience

PhD in a technical field with research related to analytics
Experience in higher education enrollment management, admission, financial aid, or institutional research analytics
Experience with Slate or a comparable higher education CRM data model

Experience mentoring or leading analysts

Knowledge of student information systems (PeopleSoft preferred) and higher education CRM systems (Slate preferred).
Knowledge of enrollment funnel concepts, including inquiry, application, admission, yield, deposit, and melt.
Knowledge of FERPA and responsible data practices for student data.
Ability to derive insight from large amounts of data and disparate sources.
Ability to communicate well verbally and in writing, presenting complex data insights to non-technical stakeholders.

jobs.title: Data Scientist
jobs.description:
Wall Township, NJ, US

French & Parrello Associates (FPA) is seeking a Data Scientist to join our team at our headquarters in Wall Township, NJ. This is an exciting opportunity for an analytical and technically driven professional to apply data science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and automation technologies to support business operations and decision-making across a growing engineering and consulting firm.

Recognized year after year as one of NJBIZ's Best Places to Work in New Jersey, FPA is committed to creating a culture where talented professionals are empowered to grow, collaborate, and succeed. In 2026, FPA was ranked #49 on Zweig's Hot Firm List, recognizing the firm among the 100 fastest-growing AEC firms in the United States and Canada. Our continued growth is driven by our investment in our people, technical excellence, and commitment to delivering innovative solutions for the communities we serve.

The successful candidate will leverage programming, database management, statistical analysis, and emerging technologies to develop data-driven solutions that improve operational efficiency and support informed business decisions. This individual will work with financial, project, operational, and external-source data to build data pipelines, develop analytical tools, implement AI and machine-learning solutions, and automate internal business processes.

This role offers the opportunity to work across multiple areas of the organization, collaborate with IT, management, and business teams, and contribute to the development of innovative technology solutions that support FPA's continued growth.

Data Science, Technology & Business Intelligence

FPA is focused on leveraging technology, data analytics, and automation to improve business processes, strengthen operational performance, and support strategic decision-making.

The Data Scientist will play an important role in developing and maintaining data infrastructure, creating business intelligence tools, and implementing artificial intelligence and machine-learning applications. This position requires a combination of programming, analytical, problem-solving, and technical skills, along with the ability to translate business needs into practical and scalable technology solutions.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, and optimize enterprise data structures and relational database systems supporting financial, project, operational, and external-source data, with an emphasis on scalability, reliability, accessibility, and system performance.
Develop and maintain SQL- and Python-based data pipelines to collect, extract, transform, validate, reconcile, organize, and synchronize data across internal business systems and external sources.
Apply statistical analysis and predictive modeling to identify trends, forecast business and project outcomes, evaluate risk and uncertainty, and support data-driven management decisions.
Develop business intelligence dashboards, tracking systems, key performance indicators (KPIs), data visualizations, and analytical reports to monitor project delivery, financial performance, operational efficiency, and business outcomes.
Design, implement, and evaluate artificial intelligence and machine-learning solutions, including predictive models, natural language processing (NLP) applications, large language model (LLM) tools, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows, and semantic and lexical information-retrieval systems.
Automate business processes and develop internal applications involving data capture, approval routing, system integration, validation controls, exception handling, process monitoring, and audit logging.
Collaborate with IT, management, and business teams to understand operational requirements and translate them into scalable technical solutions.
Establish and maintain appropriate data governance practices, technical documentation, access controls, permission structures, security configurations, and automation governance standards.
Evaluate emerging technologies, tools, and methodologies to identify opportunities to improve data management, business intelligence, and organizational efficiency.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Data Science, or a related engineering field.
Six months of relevant professional or internship experience in systems engineering, data analysis, engineering technology, IT, or a related field.
Experience or demonstrated proficiency with Python programming and SQL.
Knowledge of ETL pipeline development, data integration, and data validation processes.
Familiarity with database schema design, relational database management, and performance optimization.
Experience or knowledge of HTML and PHP.
Understanding of machine-learning pipeline development, experimental methods, A/B testing, and model evaluation.
Experience with data visualization, analytical reporting, and business intelligence tools.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across technical and nontechnical teams.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in a collaborative team environment.

The FPA Difference

Large firms offer scale. FPA offers opportunity.

For more than 50 years, French & Parrello Associates (FPA) has been delivering innovative engineering solutions that shape communities, improve infrastructure, and support regional growth. As an employee-owned, mid-sized engineering and consulting firm, FPA combines the technical capabilities and expertise of a larger organization with the collaboration, accessibility, and personal investment of a close-knit team.

At FPA, professionals are empowered to take ownership of their work, collaborate across disciplines, and contribute to meaningful initiatives that support the firm's continued growth. Your career is not defined by one task or limited to one area of expertise. Instead, you will have the opportunity to strengthen your technical skills, explore emerging technologies, work alongside experienced professionals, and develop solutions that make a measurable impact across the organization.

Our multidisciplinary approach allows team members to see the bigger picture, collaborate with experts across multiple disciplines, and understand how their work impacts the communities we serve. We invest in our people through mentorship, professional development, and opportunities for advancement because we believe the success of our employees drives the continued success of our firm.

At FPA, you are not just developing data solutions, you are helping build a growing organization through technology, innovation, and smarter business practices.

Benefits

Benefit packages for this role will start on the 1st day of employment and include medical, dental, and vision insurance, as well as HSA, FSA, and DCFSA account options, and 401k retirement plans. Employees in this role are also entitled to paid sick leave and/or other paid time off as provided by applicable law.

Compensation

The projected compensation range for this position is $87,500 to $117,000. Actual compensation will depend on factors including experience, education, qualifications, and skill set. FPA recognizes and rewards performance through an annual bonus program.

jobs.title: Data & AI Solution Architect - North America
jobs.description:
What We’re All About.

Do you ever have the urge to do things better than the last time? We do. And it’s this urge that drives us every day. Our environment of discovery and innovation means we’re able to create deep and valuable relationships with our clients to create real change for them and their industries. It’s what got us here – and it’s what will make our future. At Quantexa, you’ll experience autonomy and support in equal measures allowing you to form a career that matches your ambitions. 41% of our colleagues come from an ethnic or religious minority background. We speak over 20 languages across our 47 nationalities, creating a sense of belonging for all.

We're heading in one direction, the future. We’d love you to join us.

The opportunity

Quantexa’s largest customer engagements are now enterprise platform transformations, and North America is one of the biggest opportunities for repeating that success. As a Data & AI Solution Architect, you will be the regional technical voice for our Data & AI and Context Layer propositions. You will work with sales, field engineering, partners and customers across the region to win, shape and deliver platform opportunities.

The role combines business solutions, data architecture and AI. You will design the data foundation that makes our customers’ Data & AI and Context Layer ambitions work. You will help customers move from business use cases to the data foundation that supports them. You will also bring what you learn in the market back into our propositions and products. It is a customer-facing role with a regional focus: you will work with account teams, alliance partners, analysts and the wider Data & AI Platform Solutions community, and you will represent Quantexa publicly in North America. You will take the business use cases identified with customers, in banking, government, insurance and wider markets, and turn them into data products, models and platform architectures that can deliver them. You will work closely with the Business Solutions architects, field engineers and sales to shape large platform deals. You will also work with the technical teams at our data platform and hyperscaler partners, so that our designs fit the platforms our customers already use.

You will report to VP of Data & AI Platform Engineering and work closely with NA Head of Data & AI.

What You’ll Be Doing

Turn business use cases into data foundations

Work with the Business Solutions architects to translate customer use cases into the data products, data models and platform capabilities needed to support them.
Define and design data products, including their scope, ownership, interfaces and quality expectations.
Design data models and entity-centric structures that bring together data from many source systems.

Design data platform architectures

Design and maintain reference architectures for data integration, data products, metadata and secure deployment, for priority industries and use cases.
Position Quantexa and the Context Layer within customers’ existing data estates and target-state platforms.
Advise on data and metadata management, covering lineage, cataloguing, governance and how metadata supports the Context Layer and AI use cases.

Grow revenue through alliances and channel partners

Work with the Alliances team on co-sell opportunities with data platform, hyperscaler and systems integrator partners in the region.
Work with technical teams at data platform and hyperscaler partners, such as Databricks, Snowflake and the major cloud providers, on integration patterns and joint solution designs.
Build the architectures, accelerators and demos that show how Quantexa runs alongside these platforms. Work with the Alliances team, who lead the partner relationships, to make sure technical designs support the joint propositions.

Contribute to a reusable platform method

Help build and refine the platform methodology and toolkit, covering the data foundation steps in particular: data product definition, modelling approaches, metadata standards and platform integration patterns.
Turn what you learn on customer engagements into reusable assets, such as data product templates, model patterns and reference architectures.
Help colleagues, partners and customers use the method themselves, through guidance, workshops and materials.

Support customers and strategic deals

Run data architecture workshops with customers’ data, engineering and architecture teams.
Work with sales and field engineering to shape opportunities from early engagement through proof of concept, and provide the data architecture input to proposals.
Hand clear designs and roadmaps to delivery teams, so customers start from a strong position.

Help shape the product

Capture the features, gaps and needs that data platform integrations and customer engagements expose, and share them to inform platform strategy.
Help define product requirements for data products, metadata, integration and platform support, working with Product Management to support the product roadmap.
Work with Product, Innovation and Delivery to test new platform uses, including agentic AI, and to turn proven ideas into reusable solutions.
Build prototypes and demos, including with AI coding tools.

Support go-to-market and grow pipeline

Act as the subject-matter expert for Data & AI and Context Layer opportunities, supporting sales and field engineering from early qualification through discovery, proof of concept and proposal.
Shape opportunities with customers’ business, data and technology leaders, and help build the business case.
Run workshops that turn business use cases into a clear data and AI architecture and a roadmap for the customer.

Grow revenue through alliances and channel partners

Work with the Alliances team on co-sell opportunities with data platform, hyperscaler and systems integrator partners in the region.
Provide technical input to joint solutions, demos and account plans, so that partner conversations lead to qualified opportunities.
Help partners and channel teams position and design Quantexa solutions themselves.

Build market eminence

Engage with industry analysts and help prepare briefings, evaluations and input to research.
Speak at customer, partner and industry events, and contribute to thought leadership such as articles, blogs and webinars on enterprise data platforms, data products and AI.
Be a credible public voice for the Context Layer and enterprise AI in North America.

Support product and solution development

Bring customer, partner and analyst feedback to Product, Innovation and the platform team, and help shape priorities.
Contribute to reusable assets: reference architectures, solution patterns, demos and a repeatable platform method.
Test new platform uses, including agentic AI, and help turn proven ideas into solutions.

Lead customer engagement through go-to-market and delivery

Lead technical engagement with customers from first conversation to value realisation, working with delivery teams to carry designs and roadmaps through to implementation.
Stay close to customer outcomes after the sale, supporting expansion into further use cases.

What You’ll Bring

Experience as a solution, data or enterprise architect designing enterprise data or AI solutions, ideally in banking, insurance, government or another regulated sector.
Strong customer engagement skills with business and technical leaders, including running workshops.

A blend of skills across three areas:

business solutions: turning business problems and use cases into solution designs
data architecture: data products, data modelling, metadata and data platforms
AI: how AI and agentic approaches depend on a strong data foundation
Experience supporting sales cycles as a pre-sales or solution consulting specialist.
Familiarity with the data platform and hyperscaler ecosystems (for example Databricks, Snowflake, AWS, Azure and Google Cloud) and with working alongside partners and systems integrators.
Confidence presenting to large audiences, ideally with experience of speaking at events or working with analysts.
Comfort with product feedback: you can describe customer needs clearly and work with product teams.
A hands-on approach: you can build demos or prototypes as well as design them, ideally using AI coding tools such as Claude.
Willingness to travel across North America.

Nice to have

Knowledge of entity resolution, graph data or knowledge-graph approaches.
Domain knowledge in areas such as financial crime, customer intelligence, risk or public-sector data sharing.
Experience building reusable assets or methods for field teams.

Our perks and quirks.

What makes you Q will help you to realize your full potential, flourish and enjoy what you do, while being recognized and rewarded with our broad range of benefits.

We Offer

Our mission.

We have one mission. To help businesses grow. To make data easier. And to make the world a better place. We’re not a start-up. Not anymore. But we’ve not been around that long either. What we are is a collection of bright, passionate minds harnessing complexities and helping our clients and their communities. One culture, made of many. Heading in one direction – the future.

It’s All About You.

We want you to feel welcome, valued, and respected - because it’s your individuality and passion that make you Q . We see that, and we celebrate it. That’s why we’re proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse work environment, continuously improving to ensure everyone belongs. Our recruitment process is designed to be inclusive and accessible. No matter your race, beliefs, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, neurodiversity, or abilities—whoever you are—if you're a passionate, curious, and caring human eager to push the boundaries of what’s possible, we want to hear from you.

new_jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist, AWS Elemental
new_jobs.description:
Description

AWS Elemental builds media services used by broadcasters, streaming platforms, and sports leagues to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video. Elemental Inference is the applied machine learning team within that organization. We develop models that understand and transform live and file-based video, producing capabilities such as intelligent reframing, highlight detection, video enhancement, and contextual metadata for advertising and content discovery. Our work reaches customers through the same media workflows that carry major live events, always-on channels, and large on-demand libraries.

As a Senior Applied Scientist, you will develop new machine learning approaches and carry the strongest ideas into production. Current work spans multimodal video, audio, and language models; spatial and temporal understanding; active-speaker and point-of-interest detection; scene retrieval; video super-resolution; and learned methods for improving compression. These problems rarely have a single accepted metric or a ready-made dataset. You will help define the task itself, determine what evidence is needed, and build evaluation methods that reflect the experience of people watching and working with the resulting video.

This role combines applied research with the practical demands of a real-time media service. You will design datasets and objectives, train models at scale, run controlled comparisons, and investigate failures. You will also work closely with engineers to export, optimize, and deploy those models. A result is not finished when it performs well in a notebook. It must preserve its quality after conversion, fit within GPU memory, meet latency and throughput targets, handle the temporal behavior of live video, and operate at a cost customers can sustain.

You will be a technical leader on the team as well as an individual contributor. The role calls for someone who can take an ambiguous customer problem, separate the scientific questions from the engineering constraints, and lead a team toward a defensible answer. You will review experiments and models, mentor other scientists and engineers, and improve the shared methods the team uses for training and evaluation. Strong judgment matters here. So does the ability to explain a complicated result clearly, including its limitations, to people from several disciplines.

We welcome candidates with deep experience in computer vision, multimodal learning, video processing, or related areas. Direct media experience is valuable but not required. A scientist who has solved difficult problems in another field, understands how to test ideas rigorously, and wants to learn the video domain can also succeed in this role.

Key job responsibilities

Lead the formulation of ambiguous video problems into research plans with clear datasets, objectives, baselines, evaluation protocols, and production acceptance criteria.

Develop models for multimodal video understanding and generation, spatial and temporal reasoning, detection and tracking, scene retrieval, video enhancement, and learned compression.

Develop models for multimodal video understanding and description, spatial and temporal reasoning, detection and tracking, scene retrieval, video enhancement, and learned compression.

Build evaluations that measure the behavior customers will see. Depending on the problem, this may include task accuracy, factual support, temporal localization, retrieval quality, perceptual video quality, rate-distortion performance, or human review.

Take models from research code to production-ready artifacts. Partner with engineers on model export, reduced-precision inference, quantization, numerical parity, accelerator-specific optimization, and integration with serving systems and video pipelines.

Balance model quality against latency, throughput, GPU memory, context limits, and operating cost. Diagnose problems across training stability, data quality, precision, compilation, serving, and live temporal behavior.

Build reusable mechanisms for dataset management, experimentation, model comparison, regression detection, and performance measurement rather than solving each research problem in isolation.

Review scientific work and production code. Identify weak comparisons, data leakage, unsupported conclusions, untested edge cases, and operational risks before they reach customers.

Work with product managers, software engineers, and other scientists to make scope and design decisions. Use evidence to resolve disagreement and communicate what is known, what remains uncertain, and what further work is worth doing.

Mentor scientists and engineers in experimental design, machine learning methods, video evaluation, and production ML practices.

Contribute applied research through internal technical reports, patents, and publications at appropriate conferences or workshops.

About The Team

AWS Elemental provides a portfolio of cloud media services built to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video at global scale. Our technology supports some of the world's largest live broadcasts as well as 24/7 channels and on-demand content. The broader organization brings together expertise in video coding, image processing, distributed systems, advertising, and the operational demands of professional media.

Elemental Inference applies machine learning across that video pipeline. The team works on video understanding and enhancement, contextual metadata, smart composition, event detection, retrieval, and compression. Some projects use large multimodal models that combine video, audio, and language. Others use specialized temporal or spatial models designed for a narrow task and a strict real-time budget. We choose the approach that fits the customer problem rather than forcing every problem into the same model family.

Scientists on the team own more than model architecture. They build and govern datasets, develop annotation methods, train on distributed GPU infrastructure, and create evaluations that can reveal where a model succeeds or fails. They compare internal models with external alternatives and track accuracy, perceptual quality, latency, memory use, and cost. When a model is ready to ship, scientists work with engineers to convert it into a verified production artifact and integrate it into the inference service or the underlying video-processing engine.

Basic Qualifications

PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience
Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with modeling tools such as R, scikit-learn, Spark MLLib, MxNet, Tensorflow, numpy, scipy etc.
Experience with large scale distributed systems such as Hadoop, Spark etc.

new_jobs.title: Senior Applied Scientist, Last Hundred Yards
new_jobs.description:
Description

Every doorstep is different. Our robot has to understand all of them.

We're building robots to deliver packages to customer homes. To make that possible, we're creating a system that can automatically generate a simulation-ready digital twin of the outdoor delivery environment for every customer home Amazon delivers to; modeling the driveways, yards, walkways, stairs, porches, and doorsteps a robot must understand and navigate.

And the goal isn't simply to create virtual worlds that look real. They need to be real in the ways that matter to a robot. Geometry, semantics, appearance, physical properties, and the varied environmental cues that influence perception, planning, and motion, must be reproduced faithfully so robot behaviors from the field are repeatable in simulation.

Our simulator becomes an effective tool to study the problem. The same autonomy software that runs on the physical robot also runs in simulation. When robot behavior differs between simulation and reality, we can ask why, and improve the representation, simulation, or models that produced the difference.

Our North Star ambition is a system capable of modeling the delivery environment for every customer home we serve, across the enormous diversity of real residential environments.

There isn't an established recipe for doing this. We are advancing the knowledge frontier of scene reconstruction. The right representation may combine classical geometry, learned scene representations, generative models, world models, or approaches that haven't been invented yet.

We're interested in people with deep expertise in one or more areas of: Computer vision, 3D graphics, scene reconstruction, physics simulation, neural scene representations, Gaussian splatting, generative AI, world models, or related areas - with a strong interest in applying that expertise to robotics.

Role Overview

This is applied research with a short distance from idea conception to physical consequence. You'll work closely with robotics, autonomy, simulation, and software engineers to turn promising methods into systems that change how real robots perceive, plan, and navigate at Amazon scale.

As a Sr. Applied Scientist on the Last Mile Robotics team, you will develop cutting-edge methods for capturing, reconstructing, and simulating real-world delivery environments in high-fidelity 3D. Your work will directly enable autonomous robots to understand and navigate the diverse conditions found at customer doorsteps. You will push the boundaries of scene reconstruction, neural rendering, and generative modeling, transforming scientific breakthroughs into physical impact through rapid experimentation and close collaboration with robotics, autonomy, and simulation teams.

Basic Qualifications

Experience in applied research

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of programming languages such as C/C++, Python, Java or Perl

new_jobs.description:
About The Team

OpenAI’s Applied AI Engineering team helps organizations turn frontier AI capabilities into safe, reliable, and high-impact production systems. We work with customer executives, product and engineeriIng teams, security leaders, and transformation teams to identify valuable opportunities, accelerate technical implementation, and scale what works. Enterprise deployments are defined by complexity rather than any one industry: existing architectures, diverse data environments, security and governance requirements, multiple stakeholder groups, and organization-wide change. We turn lessons from these deployments into better products and reusable patterns for customers everywhere.

About The Role

As a Mid-Market Enterprise Applied AI Engineer you will partner directly with organizations to design, build, and deploy AI systems that deliver measurable business outcomes. You will combine deep technical judgment, hands-on engineering, and customer leadership to take ambitious ideas from use-case selection and architecture through prototyping, evaluation, production launch, and scale. You will write and debug code, build evaluation systems, resolve complex integrations, and guide decisions involving model behavior, reliability, latency, cost, safety, security, governance, and operational readiness. Success is measured by production systems, sustained adoption, and meaningful customer impact—not simply activity or successful demonstrations.

This is a rare opportunity to work as one of the early hires for a new segment within Applied AI Engineering, contributing real-world deployments at the frontier of AI while directly influencing how OpenAI’s products evolve.

This role is based in our SF or NYC office. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In This Role, You Will

Partner directly with enterprise customers to identify high-value opportunities and translate them into technical architectures, implementation plans, evaluation strategies, and measurable success criteria.
Design, build, and deploy AI systems that solve important customer problems and produce measurable business outcomes.
Work hands-on in code to build prototypes, evaluation harnesses, reference implementations, integrations, and production accelerators.
Make sound technical decisions across models, agents, retrieval, tools, data, reliability, observability, latency, cost, safety, security, and governance.
Diagnose complex implementation challenges, reproduce failures, test hypotheses, and drive blockers toward resolution.
Help customers progress from promising prototypes to reliable production systems, sustained adoption, and scaled impact.
Partner closely with customer engineering teams and OpenAI Product, Research, Engineering, Security, and go-to-market teams, translating deployment experience into high-signal product feedback.
Create reusable architectures, tooling, playbooks, and technical guidance that accelerate future enterprise deployments.

You’ll Thrive In This Role If You

Have a demonstrated track record of designing, building, and delivering AI or machine-learning systems in enterprise environments, including taking systems from prototype to production. Relevant backgrounds may include applied AI or ML engineering, forward-deployed engineering, software engineering, customer engineering, solutions architecture, or technical consulting.
Can point to substantial personal contributions in code, architecture, evaluation, debugging, or production engineering—not only program or stakeholder management.
Are highly proficient in Python and comfortable working across an AI application stack; experience with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another relevant language is valuable.
Understand how to evaluate AI systems systematically using representative data, graders, production signals, and human judgment.
Have navigated enterprise production requirements such as integrations, reliability, observability, security, privacy, data governance, performance, and cost.
Can connect technical decisions to customer workflows, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.
Communicate with clarity and credibility across hands-on engineers, technical leaders, security teams, product leaders, and executives.
Bring high agency, strong technical judgment, and end-to-end ownership in ambiguous environments.
Learn quickly, challenge assumptions constructively, and collaborate with humility; experience in a particular industry or with OpenAI products is not required.

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. new_jobs.title: Sr. Software Development Engineer – AI/ML Networking Disaggregated Inference, Annapurna Labs, Annapurna Labs
new_jobs.description:
Description

Every token a large language model generates depends on data reaching the right accelerator at the right moment. As AI models outgrow any single chip, the network between accelerators becomes the bottleneck that decides how fast — and how affordably — the world's largest models can serve real users. That network layer is what our team builds.

We're in search of an engineer to work at the frontier of disaggregated inference: splitting LLM serving into separate prefill and decode pools and moving the model's KV cache between them at the absolute limit of what the hardware allows. Get it right and users get answers in milliseconds; get it wrong and the fastest accelerators in the world sit idle waiting on data. You'll own pieces of the high-speed transfer path that make the difference, and you'll measure your success in how close you run to the theoretical peak of the machine.

What We're Looking For

Strong C/C++ and a love for low-level, performance-critical systems — solid command of Linux, kernels, memory, and writing fast code. The instinct to ask "how fast could this possibly go?" and the rigor to measure it. Experience with high-speed networking or HPC interconnects (RDMA, InfiniBand, libfabric, UCX, NIXL, MPI) is valued highly; embedded-systems experience is a plus. Prior AI/ML experience is welcome but not required — if you're a great systems engineer, we'll teach you the ML side. If you like solving genuinely hard problems, working shoulder-to-shoulder with HPC and ML customers, iterating fast, and shipping at a scale few places can offer, come join us. This is a role on the leading edge of AI/ML infrastructure.

Key job responsibilities

Build and optimize the low-level data-movement software across accelerators, servers, and heterogeneous memory — over AWS's highest-performance network fabric.

Push performance to the hardware roofline: profile, find the real bottleneck, and close the gap between "it works" and "it runs as fast as physics permits."

Work across the stack — from kernel and network transport up to the inference frameworks — and partner with teams building the chips, runtime, and models.

Deliver features that run on our largest clusters, for our largest customers, serving the largest AI models in production.

A day in the life

Annapurna Labs, a crucial part of AWS, is responsible for developing hardware and software components for EC2 infrastructure. Our team focuses on building networking solutions that for Machine Learning (ML) and High-Performance Computing (HPC) workloads on AWS.

We have mixed discipline orgs, you’d be working side by side with infrastructure experts, hardware engineers, RTL engineers, scientists & architects. Our workforce spans the globe and is truly international, you’ll find yourself working side by side with individuals from numerous countries. We take mentorship seriously, you can both expect senior mentorship and will be expected to mentor new and junior engineers.

The pace is fast as we work on the latest advancements of AI/ML, but we take the time to bond as a team and enjoy the successes. We offer flexibility in working hours, and respect WLB as a core org tenet. The team enjoys working with numerous principal-level engineers and closely with directors, career growth opportunities are certainly available. This is a role where you will always be encouraged to keep learning, the AI/ML field is fast moving and constantly evolving.

About The Team

You'd be joining Annapurna Labs, an integral part of AWS. Annapurna designs the hardware and software building blocks behind EC2 — every EC2 instance runs on hardware we designed. We specialize in the chips, systems, and software that optimize the AWS customer experience, and this team sits where cutting-edge AI meets the silicon and the network underneath it.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
5+ years of programming with at least one software programming language experience
5+ years of leading design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
5+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
Experience as a mentor, tech lead or leading an engineering team
Must have C/C++ Coding Experience

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
ML Communications (NCCL, NIXL, NVSHMEM)

new_jobs.title: Ai Infrastructure Engineer
new_jobs.description:
AI Infrastructure Engineer | GPU Systems, Networking & Data Center

Amaya Cloud | Livermore, California

Openings:
Multiple positions, approximately 4 engineers
Employment:
Full-time, W-2
Work arrangement:
Hybrid, minimum 3 days per week in Livermore
Travel:
Approximately 15-20%
Reporting:
Directly to the founder

About Amaya Cloud

Amaya Cloud is a rapidly growing U.S.-based bare-metal GPU cloud provider supporting AI training, inference, and high-performance computing workloads.
We operate thousands of GPUs across data center facilities in Oakland, California; Tucson, Arizona; and Michigan, including NVIDIA H200, B200, and B300 infrastructure.
Our customers include venture-backed AI startups, AI research laboratories, and other cloud infrastructure providers.
As our infrastructure expands, we are building a strong engineering team to deploy, operate, and troubleshoot high-performance GPU clusters and supporting data center systems.
The Opportunity

We are hiring multiple hands-on AI Infrastructure Engineers
with complementary technical specializations across networking, GPU systems, Linux, hardware, and data center operations.
We are looking for engineers with strong technical depth in one or more of these areas, rather than expecting every candidate to be an expert in everything.
You will work closely with the founding team, take ownership of complex production infrastructure problems, and help establish engineering processes as the company scales.
For experienced engineers with demonstrated leadership ability, there is an opportunity to advance into a technical lead position.
Key Responsibilities

Network Engineering and AI Fabrics

Configure and troubleshoot production L2/L3 networks, BGP, routing, VLANs, LACP, MLAG, firewalls, VPNs, and tenant connectivity.
Deploy and maintain high-speed Ethernet, InfiniBand, and RoCE fabrics, including NVIDIA/Mellanox switches and adapters.
Diagnose link failures, degraded optics, routing issues, packet loss, congestion, and RDMA performance problems.
Maintain network redundancy, segmentation, monitoring, topology documentation, and operational reliability.

GPU Systems and Linux Infrastructure

Administer and troubleshoot NVIDIA GPU servers, including H200, B200, B300, or comparable platforms.
Diagnose hardware and GPU faults using nvidia-smi, DCGM, XID logs, NVLink/NVSwitch diagnostics, and vendor tooling.
Maintain Linux operating systems, GPU drivers, CUDA dependencies, NVIDIA Fabric Manager, and compatible firmware versions.
Support bare-metal provisioning, host configuration, storage administration, and infrastructure automation.
Perform GPU cluster validation, including NCCL, bandwidth, and performance diagnostics.

Server Hardware and Data Center Operations

Diagnose server hardware failures using BMC/IPMI logs, MCE/EDAC events, memory diagnostics, and vendor troubleshooting tools.
Coordinate server deployments, hardware replacements, RMA processes, and equipment maintenance.
Support rack installations, fiber and copper cabling, power distribution, redundant A/B feeds, and rack-level power capacity planning.
Troubleshoot airflow, cooling, thermal conditions, and environmental issues affecting equipment reliability.
Maintain asset inventory, cabling records, rack diagrams, and operational documentation.
Support networked and high-performance storage systems and diagnose connectivity, performance, and hardware issues.

Reliability and Engineering Ownership

Own assigned infrastructure incidents through diagnosis, resolution, root-cause analysis, and preventive action.
Build monitoring, alerts, runbooks, and automation to improve infrastructure reliability.
Coordinate with colocation providers, remote-hands teams, vendors, and internal engineers.
Participate in planned maintenance, deployment windows, and shared on-call coverage.
Lead technical initiatives, mentor colleagues, and contribute to engineering standards and processes.

Required Qualifications

4+ years of relevant hands-on experience in production infrastructure, data centers, network engineering, Linux systems, or hardware operations.
Strong demonstrated technical expertise in at least one of the following:

Production networking, routing, switching, and high-speed fabrics.
NVIDIA GPU infrastructure, Linux systems, and server provisioning.
Enterprise server hardware diagnostics, data center deployment, and physical infrastructure.
Cross-functional infrastructure operations, automation, and production incident management.
Practical troubleshooting experience in production environments.
Working knowledge of Linux, server hardware, and basic networking concepts.
Ability to diagnose complex problems independently and document technical findings.
Strong communication, accountability, and ability to collaborate across technical disciplines.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with InfiniBand, RoCE, RDMA, UFM, OFED, or NVIDIA networking.
Experience with GPU diagnostics, DCGM, CUDA, NCCL, NVLink, or NVSwitch.
Experience with BMC/IPMI, Redfish, server firmware, memory diagnostics, and hardware failure analysis.
Familiarity with bare-metal provisioning tools such as MAAS, Foreman, or Ironic.
Experience with high-performance storage such as NVMe, NFS, Lustre, WEKA, or similar platforms.
Experience with Python, Bash, Ansible, Prometheus, Grafana, or similar automation and observability tools.
Experience with high-density or liquid-cooled data center infrastructure.
Technical leadership, mentoring, or project ownership experience.

Location and Working Requirements

Must currently be located in the San Francisco Bay Area within practical commuting distance of Livermore.
Available to work at least three days per week in the Livermore office and visit data center facilities as needed.
Available for approximately 15-20% business travel.
Reliable transportation for regional site visits.
Available for occasional after-hours maintenance and a shared on-call rotation.
Able to perform essential data center duties with or without reasonable accommodation, including safely handling equipment weighing up to 50 pounds, with appropriate lifting assistance when needed.

Work Authorization and Hiring Process

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. Amaya Cloud does not offer employment visa sponsorship for these positions.
Finalists may be asked to provide professional references and complete legally compliant employment verification and background screening.
New hires participate in a paid 30-day onboarding and initial performance evaluation, followed by formal performance and development reviews at six and twelve months.
Why Join Amaya Cloud?

Work directly with the founding team:
Take part in technical decisions and help build the company's engineering organization.
Rapid growth:
Join a scaling AI infrastructure provider with meaningful engineering challenges and new deployments.
Advanced technology:
Gain hands-on experience with NVIDIA GPU systems, high-performance networking, and modern data center infrastructure.
Professional development:
Opportunities for company-supported technical certifications, training, and industry events, subject to approval.
Career progression:
Opportunities to take on larger technical responsibilities and potentially advance into engineering leadership.

Amaya Cloud is an equal opportunity employer and provides reasonable accommodation in accordance with applicable law.
